example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, seven balance sheet accounts, 30 September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.Miscellaneous expense: the name of the user's own P&L account for approved write-offs. The page gives no account name

messages.text: Can you reconcile our balance sheet accounts for September?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need eight answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which company? For a group, which entities?
Which accounts? Name them, or say all balance sheet accounts.
Which period end? I never assume one.
Some support is outside the books, such as prepaid, fixed asset, loan and accrual schedules. Can you attach each one?
What size of difference must you resolve at once? I can suggest a basis, but you choose the threshold.
Do you have last period's reconciliation?
messages.after: The last two are optional, but they make the work stronger.

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading. Payroll clearing, A/R, A/P, prepaid, accrued expenses, fixed assets and the term loan. Period end 30 September. Schedules attached, but the fixed asset register is not ready. $500 per account. No rec for August. The bookkeeper prepares, the controller reviews.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan for the **Northbrook Trading** workspace and company file. I reconcile **seven accounts** at **30 September**, with your general ledger (GL) read through MosoFin. I tie A/R and A/P to their agings and test them against receipts and payments after the date. Payroll clearing must be zero. Your schedules support prepaid, accrued expenses and the loan. The fixed asset register is missing, so fixed assets show as **not reconciled**. Materiality is **$500**.
messages.after: One question before I start. A small residual can get a write-off, but only below a limit that you approve. What is that limit, and which P&L account takes it?

messages.text: Up to $100, to Miscellaneous expense. Then go ahead.

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Five open lines in payroll clearing
Entries to A/R without a customer
messages.summary: 10 reads in one batch. All live data, no mock. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: I start with the clearing account. Payroll clearing 2200 must be zero. It shows **$4,023.40** in five open lines:
messages.after: The $23.40 is more than a year old. That usually means nobody owns the account. I do not roll an open clearing balance forward. The payroll lead owns each line, with a target date of Fri 16 Oct.

messages.text: Accounts receivable is **$750** away from its aging:
messages.after: The aging comes from the same books, so this tie is only a mechanical check. The independent test is the receipts after the date. Customers paid $31,400 of the 30 September invoices from 1 to 9 October. I found no late entries, no foreign currency and no rounding. A journal entry to A/R without a customer is the likely cause. The $750 is above $500, so it needs resolution now. The bookkeeper owns it, with a target date of Fri 9 Oct.

messages.text: Can you post the $750 to suspense so the account ties?

No. I never plug a difference, and I never write to your books. The $750 is also above your $100 write-off limit. A write-off never goes to a suspense account on the balance sheet. A/R stays **Investigating** until the bookkeeper finds the cause.
Prepaid expenses show **$22,100**. Your schedule shows **$14,850**. Three errors explain the difference:

card.title: Prepaid expenses
rows: − Refundable landlord deposit, reclass to a deposits asset

messages.after: Each item is permanent, so each one gets a proposed entry. None of them is timing.

messages.text: Accrued expenses 2110 show **$27,790**. Your schedules support **$25,750**: AP cutoff $14,650, electricity $2,100 and audit fees $9,000. With no August rec, I start from the 31 August balance as I read it today.
messages.after: The August accrual of $2,040 should reverse on Tue 1 Sep. No reduction is there, so the $2,040 is a permanent item. Nothing in August changed after you closed it, so I raise no prior-period flag.

messages.text: I propose four entries. Each one points to its evidence:

card.title: Proposed entries
head: Entry
Amount
Evidence
rows: Reclass the landlord deposit to a deposits asset
Reverse the August accrual: Dr 2110 Accrued expenses, Cr 6310 Utilities

messages.after: The four entries total **$9,290**. A person posts them. I do not. Prepaid and accrued expenses are reconciled only when the entries are posted.

messages.text: Here is the coverage sheet. Each account shows how I got each side:

card.title: Coverage, 30 September
head: Account
GL balance
Support
Status
rows: Same books, receipts after the date
Same books, payments $41,200 after the date

messages.after: Support with evidence covers **79.2%** of the $607,313.40 in scope. Fixed assets stay not reconciled until the controller supplies the register.

messages.text: Your workpaper has one tab for each account and the coverage sheet. The bookkeeper prepares it, and the controller reviews it.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Here is **BS_Recs_2026-09_Northbrook Trading.xlsx**. I saved the source for each account, the $500 threshold and the 3-month escalation. I also saved the people, the $100 limit with Miscellaneous expense, and payroll clearing as an account that must be zero. I never save balances, item detail or the workpaper.
